stage: integration (diarrhea) check of the 8 absorb components against the OAW V2 reference
method: Read-only review of OAW code, tests, templates, policy and eval runners. No food code was run. Two local measurements were made with ~/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python313/python.exe -I -B, using scripts written outside both trees in scratchpad/integ-tools/: (1) the scripts+templates tree digest, recomputed as 92b7f3d8... against the a4ee3c46... frozen in evals/egm-pilot/spec.json and evals/egm-local/spec.json, so those historical registrations already reject current source by design (tests/test_egm_local.py test_current_source_cannot_run_historical_contract); (2) the stdlib import closure of the installed helpers on Python 3.13/Windows: 50 stdlib top-level names for context_hub, 55 with improvement, wiki_sync and validate_skills, against the 290-name sys.stdlib_module_names.
shared_findings: Any change to scripts/context_hub.py, scripts/oaw_common.py, scripts/improvement.py or templates/ requires `python scripts/sync_examples.py --write`. Otherwise harness_check 'example-content' fails, because example/minimal-project and example/public-hybrid-demo carry byte copies of context_hub.py, oaw_common.py, improvement.py and oaw-evidence/SKILL.md.

Changing scripts/ or templates/ changes the oaw_source tree digest. The egm-pilot and egm-local registrations are already historical (frozen digest a4ee3c46... vs current 92b7f3d8...), so nothing in the gate regresses, but any future paid A/B for these absorbs needs a fresh registration with its own hash.

Installed projects receive the new helpers through migrate: an unmodified managed file updates, a user-edited one becomes a conflict proposal. No legacy_manifest change is needed (it lists only v1 hashes).

The D3 attribution goes in docs/releases/<ver>-sources.json. harness_check version_check rejects any source without a full 40-hex commit: use 02584c4ac9d92fea45adf5c61e22c546b5738621 and the Apache-2.0 root paths only (never cowork/).

None of the 8 absorbs adds a skill, changes a skill description, adds startup-loaded text, a hook, a dependency or a network call. The EGM bridges are manual-only (disable-model-invocation: true and allow_implicit_invocation: false, pinned by test_native_bridges_keep_manual_invocation_policy_for_both_hosts), so no absorb can steal an EGM trigger.

Two absorbs edit the same function (_render_recall/memory_recall). Ledger claim checked: 'default output unchanged, parity by construction' (cm.recall-index-first) stops being true once cm.recall-data-fence lands, because the fence changes default output.

checks.other_parts_regress: The CLI half is safe if --index is a separate mode that reuses the cursor and max_chars machinery. Tests that guard the default path: tests/test_context_hub.py test_recall_budgets_json_and_pages_independent_entries, test_recall_text_is_bounded_and_cursor_detects_changes and test_recall_trims_expensive_prefix_before_the_query_match. Also harness cli-contracts (context_hub.py --help must still list memory/search) and example-content (the synced copy of context_hub.py and oaw-evidence/SKILL.md). Two gaps need new tests. (1) The cursor packs [1, index, query_hash, snapshot] (context_hub.py:348-366), so an --index cursor would be accepted by a default-mode call on the same query and silently page a different row shape; the mode must go into the hashed tuple, with a test that a cross-mode cursor is refused. (2) Knowledge pages (docs/knowledge/*.md) have no '## [date] [TAG]' header, so their index row needs the page title or the matched line, not 'first line'. The rule at context_hub.py:471 that every excerpt carries its full match has no index counterpart yet; one has to be defined (for example, the row cites the line of the match).
checks.trigger_conflict: None. No new skill, and the oaw-evidence description (its trigger) stays unchanged. Only the on-demand body would change.
checks.context_budget: Startup cost is zero. The proposed SKILL.md line adds about 150 bytes to an on-demand body of 1,110 bytes, loaded only when oaw-evidence triggers. Index rows cost less per hit than 2,000-char excerpts, but the token saving is the food's own unmeasured claim.
checks.instruction_conflict: The CLI flag is consistent with templates/AGENTS.md:9 (load notes only when needed). The SKILL.md line ('for broad queries take --index first, then Read the cited line') is a skill-behavior change. It can add a second tool call and turn per lookup, and the README's proof-before-promotion principle (README.md:46,143) asks for matched A/B evidence before a skill change is accepted. The ledger holds the analogous one-line trigger (cm.file-touch-recall-trigger) for exactly this reason, so shipping this line at 'parity' unmeasured is inconsistent.
checks.cross_host: The CLI is identical on Claude Code and Codex: one stdlib script, and oaw-evidence installs from one source to both .agents/skills and .claude/skills (test_each_host_gets_its_native_bridges_and_identical_shared_runtime). No counterpart is needed. Whether either host's model follows the index-first guidance is untested on both.
checks.notes: Split it. Absorb now: `memory recall --index`, with the mode bound into the cursor hash, a defined row format for knowledge pages, the full output fitted to --max-chars, and fixture byte counts recorded as static-measured evidence. Hold: the oaw-evidence SKILL.md line, until the recall A/B listed under cm.ranked-fts5-recall (or a cheaper 2-arm index-first A/B) shows parity or better on turns and tokens. Until then, document --index only in --help and docs/CLI_Reference.md:44. Also correct the ledger's parity-by-construction claim: it holds for the CLI only, and only while the fence is not added to default output.

checks.other_parts_regress: memory_add/lesson/memory_show/status/bootstrap all split entries on '^## \[' (context_hub.py:219,324,413,523,557,586), so an extra 'files:' line inside an entry body is safe. Tests that would catch damage: test_multiprocessing_memory_entries_all_survive and test_failed_mutation_preserves_original_and_releases_lock (locked RMW in memory_add), plus the three recall tests. Five regression risks need new tests. (1) `memory recall` takes a required positional query (context_hub.py:784) and memory_recall rejects an empty one (394-395), so --file needs nargs='?' plus mutual-exclusion rules, which is a CLI contract change. (2) Ranking reorders hits, so the cursor must bind mode and file path, not only the query hash, or a cursor from one ordering pages another. (3) The specificity score's '+2 if in files_modified' has no OAW analog, because --files records one undifferentiated list. (4) Text-citation matching must be path-boundary aware: scripts/oaw.py must not match scripts/oaw.py.bak. (5) The staleness flag is unsound as designed. Entries carry only a date ('%Y-%m-%d', context_hub.py:289), and git does not preserve mtime, so after any clone or checkout every file's mtime is newer than every entry. file_changed_since_entry would then be true for all hits on CI and teammates' machines, and same-day edits are ambiguous.
checks.trigger_conflict: None. No skill or description change; the trigger to call it is held separately (cm.file-touch-recall-trigger).
checks.context_budget: Zero at startup. Adds one 'files:' line per entry written with --files and a few JSON fields per hit; all on demand.
checks.instruction_conflict: Consistent with templates/AGENTS.md:14 (check an old conclusion against current code). Showing stale history with a flag, instead of hiding it, fits evidence-not-instructions. A flag that is always true after a clone would be misleading evidence, though, which conflicts with AGENTS.md:18-19 (record measured validation; do not imply what checks prove). Privacy: store paths project-relative in POSIX form. Absolute paths would leak local layout into a committed file (AGENTS.md:20-21). Note that confined_path accepts absolute in-project paths and returns them absolute, so --files must relativize after confining.
checks.cross_host: Host-independent: Python only, identical on both hosts. One cross-platform point: normalize input backslashes and match case-sensitively on every OS. Using os.path.normcase would make the same memory.md recall differently on Windows and Linux. The ranking and flag fields reach both hosts unchanged.
checks.notes: Absorb with three required changes. (1) Replace the mtime-vs-date rule with a content fingerprint: `memory add --files` records path@sha256[:12] (CRLF folded to LF, as evals/egm-pilot/pilot_common.py:39-41 already does). Recall then reports changed_since_entry as true, false or missing by rehashing the file. This is deterministic, clone-independent and testable with free fixtures. (2) Bind the mode, file and query into the cursor hash, and add a test that cross-mode cursors are refused. (3) Drop the '+2 modified' term, or add an explicit --modified list; keep the '<=3 files +2, <=8 files +1' part. Keep the query positional required for literal mode, add --file as an alternative selector, and update docs/CLI_Reference.md:44 and both example copies.

Its single-hit JSON packet is about 390 chars before the excerpt, notice included, so it still fits, but headroom at the floor shrinks by about 100 chars, and long docs/knowledge source names reach the 'too small' error (context_hub.py:485,494) sooner. No EGM bridge or gated script parses recall output. The egm-pilot arm-C overlay is historical (frozen source digest), so no live contract breaks. Add one test: the notice is present in text and JSON, counted inside --max-chars, and printed on 'No matches found.' as well.
checks.context_budget: About 90-100 chars per recall call, on demand only, counted inside the caller's --max-chars, which already bounds the full rendered output. Zero at startup.
checks.instruction_conflict: This directly implements AGENTS.md:16-17, templates/AGENTS.md:15 and README.md:142 (evidence, not instructions) at the point of output. It only repeats a rule already in oaw-evidence/SKILL.md:20-21, so it adds no new instruction. It is a one-line header, not a closed fence; JSON string quoting delimits excerpts structurally, and text mode relies on the header only. Whether the label changes model behavior is not measured; ship as 'parity, no improvement claimed'. checks.other_parts_regress: oaw_common.py is imported by context_hub, wiki_sync and improvement, and every install includes it (oaw.py:234). Adding a constant table and a pure function changes no existing behavior. The guard is called only from memory_add and annotate, and lesson inherits it. Tests to keep green: the oaw_common lock and confinement tests in tests/test_context_hub.py (test_locked_update_refuses_symlinked_target_escape, test_concurrent_readers_cannot_fail_locked_replace) and the memory/annotation tests above. Porting hazard: Python re does not support variable-width lookbehind. The food's url_credentials, aws_secret_key, aws_session_token and slack/discord webhook patterns use variable-width lookbehinds (redaction.ts:108,119,126,175-176), and a literal port raises re.error at import. That would break every helper that imports oaw_common, context_hub status in harness installed-lifecycle included. Because OAW refuses instead of redacting, rewrite them as plain consuming matches. Add one positive and one negative fixture per pattern (the negatives include the '${DB_PASS}' placeholder and an unclosed or short 'sk-' prose token), plus an import-time compile test.

The argv test in tests/ uses a mocked binary and asserts single-token empty values. One cheap person-approved live probe must assert empty tools, skills, plugins and MCP servers in the init event. checks.other_parts_regress: This is an optional field, so existing specs keep their exact verdicts: validate_spec ignores unknown keys (improvement.py:74-91), and the stored spec is hash-pinned at propose time (evaluation_sha256). Tests that pin current behavior: tests/test_improvement.py test_eligible_decision_never_applies_patch, test_no_benefit_is_inconclusive, test_per_assertion_regression_rejected_even_if_total_pass_count_equal, test_resource_regression_and_failed_checks_block_promotion, test_earlier_non_eligible_comparison_blocks_acceptance and test_evidence_changed_during_acceptance_cannot_reuse_old_comparison. Also harness installed-lifecycle (improvement.py --help) and example-content (public-hybrid-demo copy). Design trap: if the trigger is modeled as one of spec['assertions'], the baseline arm (no mechanism) fails every row. Candidate passes then exceed baseline passes (improvement.py:277,321) and the trigger itself makes the candidate 'eligible', which is the opposite of the guard. The trigger must be a separate per-case boolean, read from candidate rows only, excluded from the baseline-vs-candidate regression loop (301-304), and evaluated per designated trigger case. Pooling over all cases would let control cases (where the mechanism should not fire) dilute or mask the rate. decide() re-runs compare (375-379), so the rule also covers acceptance revalidation, which correctly fails closed.
checks.trigger_conflict: None. improvement.py is reached only through the opt-in oaw-improve skill, whose description is unchanged.
checks.instruction_conflict: Strengthens proof-before-promotion (README.md:143) and matches the pilot's verdict rules, where failed or invalid baselines never establish parity or evolution (evals/egm-pilot/spec.json verdict_rules). The docs step (a no-model preflight before any paid run) matches skill-catalog-execution.md:68 and the pilot's dry-run default. One honesty note: an older installed improvement.py silently ignores the new field, so a spec authored for the new rule can still pass vacuously on an old install. The CLI reference should state the minimum version that enforces it.
checks.cross_host: Host-independent: it compares recorded run artifacts from either host identically. No counterpart needed.
checks.notes: Absorb as an optional spec block, e.g. {"trigger": {"cases": [...], "minimum_rate": 0.667}}. Validate it with the existing number() and names() helpers (cases must be a subset of spec cases). Candidate rows carry a boolean 'triggered'. Below the rate on any designated case, the verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'vacuous: mechanism did not trigger', checked before the efficiency_gain and passed-count branches but after the 'rejected' conditions. Fixtures needed: vacuous efficiency gain leads to inconclusive; triggered gain leads to eligible; a trigger field placed under assertions is refused or ignored; specs without the block are unchanged.

checks.other_parts_regress: doctor feeds init/migrate acceptance. Tests that would catch a misfire: tests/test_install.py test_fresh_minimal_install_and_idempotence (doctor exit 0), test_explicit_keep_custom_resolves_reviewed_policy_and_stays_protected (asserts no WARN at all), test_doctor_rejects_missing_required_managed_helper, tests/test_egm_integration.py test_default_minimal_v2_includes_all_bridges_and_the_complete_runtime (doctor 'healthy'), and harness installed-lifecycle (doctor on a fresh target). These fixtures have no stray scripts/ files, so they would not catch the real problem, which is false positives in user projects. Measured: the installed helpers import 50-55 stdlib top-level names on Python 3.13 (several of them builtin or frozen and not shadowable at all), while sys.stdlib_module_names has 290. A FAIL on any stdlib stem would mark a project 'unhealthy' for harmless files such as scripts/site.py, scripts/email.py, scripts/secrets.py, scripts/profile.py, scripts/platform.py or scripts/calendar.py, none of which any OAW helper imports. Coverage gaps the other way: the rule checks only *.py. CPython's FileFinder also loads package directories (scripts/json/__init__.py, which wins over a same-name module in that directory), sourceless .pyc files and extension modules (.pyd or .so). The 'equals oaw_common' clause is vacuous for .py, because that path is the managed file itself, which doctor already hash-checks; the real vector is scripts/oaw_common/__init__.py.
checks.instruction_conflict: No host settings are touched; the check only reports (README.md:202). The ledger frames it as defense against planted code, which overstates it. doctor compares managed files against .oaw/install.json inside the same project (oaw.py:651-659), so an attacker who controls the repo can also edit the hashes. Doctor is a health check, not a security boundary. Describe the check as accidental-shadowing hygiene, to stay within 'do not imply what checks prove' (AGENTS.md:18-19).
checks.cross_host: Host-independent and identical on both hosts. Cross-platform: the import closure differs by Python version and OS (fcntl vs msvcrt, posixpath on Windows via pathlib/glob), and the harness forbids skipped tests (harness_check.py:87-88). Build fixtures from importlib.machinery suffix lists, not per-OS skips.
checks.notes: Absorb in reduced form. FAIL only when scripts/ holds a module, package directory, sourceless .pyc or extension module whose name is in the helpers' real import closure, or is oaw_common as a package. Compute that closure in an isolated subprocess at doctor time, or pin it in a test that is regenerated per supported Python. Use WARN (not FAIL) for other stdlib-named entries, and nothing for names OAW never imports. A stronger structural fix can be weighed as a separate proposal: when run as __main__, the helpers would drop their own directory from sys.path and load oaw_common by explicit path. It is not a drop-in, because tests insert scripts/ at sys.path[0] and import the helpers as modules. The Windows PATH hygiene stays excreted (OAW never edits PATH).

process_notes_for_the_digestion_system: These two absorbs feed the digestion system itself, and both need amendments before they are gate-ready. The goldfish launch recipe is gate-ready on Claude only after an init-event probe, with Codex recorded as audit-based and 'untested'. The non-vacuous rule must sit outside 'assertions', or it inverts into a free pass.

Integration found one recurring pattern in the ledger: a mechanism (CLI flag, fixture-testable) gets bundled with a model-behavior change (a skill line). Split them every time: absorb the mechanism at static evidence, hold the skill line behind the A/B. This is the rule the ledger already applied to cm.file-touch-recall-trigger.
